_meta.purpose: Compensation reference for a ~2.7-year engineer with Dev's profile. Used to sanity-check offers and to anchor recruiter conversations.
_meta.provenance: ESTIMATES, not sourced data. The automated comp-research pass did not complete (session limit). These are directional bands based on the shape of the Indian market for a 2-4 year product engineer. VERIFY every number on Levels.fyi, AmbitionBox and 6figr before you quote it in a negotiation — see data/platforms.json tier6_salary_intel.
_meta.unit: INR lakhs per annum (LPA), total fixed + typical variable, excluding equity
_meta.warning: Never treat a band here as a reason to reject a posting. Indian JDs almost never state comp, and the real number is set at the recruiter call.

devActuals.reading: His stated expectation sits BELOW the mid band for every lane here except Ahmedabad-local mobile. That is not a reason to retarget downward - it is a reason to treat 12 as a floor. A 1.23-1.34x jump under-prices a move into the AI/agentic lane, where his production agent work is genuinely scarce.

bands.note: Widest band of any lane. Well-funded AI startups pay far above the market median for engineers who have genuinely shipped agent systems — which Dev has. This is where his differentiator converts into money.
Remote-India roles at Indian AI startups track Bengaluru with a modest discount.
FDE is still a thin title in India, so the sample is small. Often carries a variable component tied to customer outcomes — clarify the fixed/variable split early.
Steady demand, deep supply. Dev's BLE/IoT and regulated-healthcare depth is what pushes him toward the upper half.
Gujarat market runs materially below the Bengaluru/Hyderabad bands. This gap is the single strongest financial argument for remote or relocation.
KMP adopters are few, so postings are rare — but the scarcity works in his favour when one appears. 'Shipped a DiGA-certified KMP app to both stores' is a rare sentence.
Highest posting volume, most competition, lowest differentiation. Treat as the fallback lane.

Roughly USD 30k-95k, usually as a contractor or via an EOR (Deel, Remote.com, Oyster). Almost always excludes Indian statutory benefits and shifts tax handling onto him. Very competitive to land, but a single such role can be worth 2-3x a local offer.

negotiationNotes: Dev's actuals: current 8.94 LPA, expected 11-12+. Anchor at 12 as the FLOOR and let them counter. Do not volunteer 8.94 until the role's own band is on the table - in India the current-CTC question exists mainly to cap the offer.

Reality check on the ask: 8.94 -> 12 is +34%. For an Ahmedabad-to-Bengaluru product-company move the normal range is 1.6-2.2x, i.e. 14-20 LPA. If an AI/agentic role comes through at 12, he has likely left money on the table - check the band on Levels.fyi before accepting.

Anchor on the ROLE's band, not on a percentage of the current salary. Indian recruiters ask for current CTC specifically to cap the offer — answer with your expected range instead wherever the form allows it.
Fill in profile.json currentCtcLPA and expectedCtcLPA. Application forms demand both constantly, and Claude must never guess them on your behalf.

The agentic-engineering work is the strongest lever Dev has. Most 2-3 year engineers cannot say they designed and operate a multi-agent delivery pipeline in production. Lead with it in the first recruiter call, not the fourth.
A jump from a Gujarat-market salary to a Bengaluru product-company band is often 1.6-2.2x. That is normal for this move, not greedy.
Ask for the fixed/variable/equity split in writing before saying yes to any number.
The two cloud certifications (AWS CCP, Azure Fundamentals) are worth mentioning but are entry-level — they will not move a band on their own. Do not over-index on them.
